name: encoding-base64mime
algorithm: Base64 decode that skips line breaks: n splitmix64 bytes (seed 1) encoded once with the standard padded alphabet and broken into lines of cols characters ending in CRLF (cols 0: no break), decoded rounds times by each language's standard decoder that skips whitespace; the checksum adds per round the decoded length and one decoded byte at a moving index (README.md).

skip.c: no base64 in C's standard library
skip.rust: no base64 in Rust's std (base64 is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

variants.name: mime76
notes: 76-column lines ending in CRLF (RFC 2045's MIME form).

variants.name: clean
notes: One line, no break: a data: URL's payload.

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the decoder is tested by the lane's Go tests (TestStdEncoding_Base64Adversarial, TestStdEncoding_ForgivingVector)
notes: Mk: Base64DecodeTo with Base64Forgiving (WHATWG forgiving-base64: skips TAB, LF, FF, CR and SPACE) into one buffer; a vector-counted shape pass, then 16-character vector blocks between line breaks (Mula and Lemire, SSSE3 at the hosted baseline). Go: encoding/base64.StdEncoding.Decode, which skips CR and LF, into one buffer. Zig: std.base64.standard.decoderWithIgnore, ignoring CR and LF, decode into one buffer.
Checksums: Go's at both sizes on the owner's machine (std-encoding fix round, 2026-11-12); Mk and Zig printed the quick checksum for both variants.
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
